Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB as many of you know us, Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Consumer Brands Inc.'s Q2 results. With me on the call are Mike Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team, including Tom Vargas, our Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Reynolds.

Mike Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Global Consumer Brands Inc. delivered a solid Q2, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover four key aspects: our organic sales growth rate, the decomposition of that growth into volume, price, and mix; geographic performance across developed and emerging markets; and our organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and full year.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $12.8 billion, representing a 6.5% increase compared to the prior year on a reported basis, with organic growth of 5.2%. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by pricing discipline, favorable mix shifts, and operational efficiencies that absorbed input cost inflation. Operating income was $2.5 billion, up 7% year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share were $1.45. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here—and thank you for joining our Q2 earnings call for Global Consumer Brands Inc. Before I dive into the segment details, let's zoom in on our organic sales growth rate, which came in at a robust 5.2% for the quarter—comfortably ahead of our guided range of 3% to 5% and marking the third consecutive quarter of acceleration. For the first half year-to-date, we're at 4.8%, putting us on track to deliver our full-year target of 4% to 6%. This is core business momentum at work, excluding a modest FX headwind from a stronger U.S. dollar, the dilutive impact from the divestiture of our low-margin European private-label snacks business earlier this year, and the small boost from the HealthSpan acquisition in North America, which we're integrating smoothly.

To break it down, our organic growth was driven by a balanced 2.1% volume increase, 1.8% net pricing, and 1.3% favorable mix shift. Volume was the standout—our strongest in two years—fueled by share gains across 70% of our $28 billion portfolio, according to Nielsen and IRI scan data. Pricing held steady as inflation cooled in most markets, allowing us to protect margins without alienating value-conscious consumers. Mix improved as we shifted toward higher-margin premium SKUs, lapping easier comps from last year's heavy promotional discounting.

Regionally, North America, our largest market at around 55% of sales, delivered 5.1% organic growth, with volume up 2.8% thanks to distribution gains in club channels like Costco and Sam's Club. Our PowerClean laundry detergent line—our biggest hero brand—gained 1.2 points of market share to 32%, thanks to the reformulation with our BioShield enzyme tech, which cuts cleaning time by 20% and resonates with busy households. Premium beauty, led by GlowEssence serums, added another 1.5 points, riding the clean beauty wave against competitors like P&G's Olay.

In EMEA, growth was 3.7%, tempered by softer UK volumes amid cost-of-living pressures, but offset by 6% pricing in Turkey and the Nordics. We expanded household penetration for FreshGuard wipes by 15% through targeted in-store sampling and TikTok Shop integrations, stealing share from Reckitt's Lysol. Sustainability played big—our EcoPack refill pouches for dish soaps hit 12% of category sales, ahead of Unilever's similar efforts.

Latin America was the standout at 7.4%, driven by 4.2% volume in Brazil and Mexico, where economic recovery and our VivaSnax portable snacks—now the #2 brand behind Mondelez's Oreo Bites—captured 250 basis points of share. We leaned into informal trade channels, which account for 40% of sales in the region, via micro-depot expansions and real-time inventory apps that cut stockouts by 30%.

Asia-Pacific clocked 2.9%, with China volumes challenged by lingering COVID effects into early Q2, but India exploding at 12% on sachet innovations for our SpiceBurst seasonings, mirroring Nestlé's Maggi success. E-commerce now represents 18% of APAC sales, up from 12% last year, powered by our Alibaba and Shopee exclusives.

Strategically, this isn't luck—it's execution on our Growth Accelerator playbook. We've rationalized 15% of our 5,000+ SKUs since 2022, focusing on 80/20 winners like PowerClean and GlowEssence, which now drive 35% of sales at twice the margins. Tech initiatives like our AI-powered demand sensing platform—integrated with SAP and built on partnerships with Palantir—improved forecast accuracy to 92%, enabling just-in-time production and reducing waste by 18%. On the consumer front, we're countering downtrading with affordable premium tiers: think $4.99 multipacks for VivaSnax, which grew 25% while everyday low-price segments declined.

Challenges include persistent input cost volatility—cocoa up 40% YTD hurting our chocolate adjacencies—and private-label aggression in Europe, where Aldi's copycats eroded 50 basis points in household care. But our everyday hero strategy and velocity merchandising—boosting shelf facings by 10% on average—held the line.

Looking forward, we see organic growth sustaining at 4% to 6% in the second half and into FY2025, with volume inflecting to 2.5%+ as inflation fully moderates. We'll lap tough comps from last year's pricing actions, but innovations like our zero-waste diaper line launching in NA soon and AI-personalized beauty via our app should more than offset. This positions us favorably versus peers—P&G at around 3.5%, Colgate at 3.2% per their recent prints—while expanding our mid-single-digit operating margin to 22%+.

Before moving on, I'd like to unpack our organic sales growth decomposition further, as this framework underscores the health and sustainability of our top-line momentum. This 5.2% organic sales growth was comprised of volume growth of +2.1%, pricing actions contributing +1.8%, and favorable mix shift of +1.3%. This is a textbook CPG decomposition, reflecting not just defensive pricing in an inflationary environment but genuine demand pull through innovation and execution. For context, this compares favorably to peers like Procter & Gamble's recent 2-4% organic prints or Unilever's 3.1% in their last quarter, where volume remains a headwind amid cost-of-living pressures.

Volume growth of +2.1% flipped from a -0.8% drag in Q1 to a solid tailwind, equating to about 1.2 percentage points of our total organic growth and broad-based across categories and regions. In Beverages, 35% of our portfolio, NARTD volume grew +3.5%, fueled by distribution gains in emerging channels like convenience stores and e-commerce. Our HydraSpark sparkling water line, with its zero-sugar, electrolyte-infused variants, saw velocity up 12% in North America, capturing share from flat soda volumes at competitors like PepsiCo's core brands. Snacks delivered +1.8% volume, with protein-packed NutriCrunch bars gaining 15% household penetration via targeted in-store demos and TikTok influencer campaigns—mirroring Mondelez's success with high-protein extensions.

Household & Personal Care lagged slightly at +0.9% volume but improved sequentially, thanks to supply chain normalization post-Red Sea disruptions. Regionally, North America contributed +2.8% volume on 4% ACV gains from shelf resets at Walmart and Kroger, while Asia-Pacific surged +4.2% on festive season prep in India and China, where our affordable sachet packs for shampoo drove trial among rural consumers. Latin America was flat at +0.1%, weighed by FX volatility but offset by strong Mexico execution. Key initiatives? Our Velocity Accelerator program—deployed across 80% of our SKU portfolio—used AI-driven planogramming to boost facings by 8% on average, directly linking to a 2.5x ROI on trade spend.

Pricing remains disciplined at +1.8%, below the category average of 2-3% but up from +1.2% in Q1 as we lap easier comps. This reflects strategic elasticity management rather than blunt inflation pass-through. In Beverages, we took modest +2.1% MSRPs on premium lines like HydraSpark to fund marketing, maintaining price gaps with mass players like Coca-Cola's Dasani. Snacks pricing was +1.5%, with temporary elasticities tested via A/B pricing in Europe, holding steady at -0.2x—better than Unilever's snack peers amid private label aggression.

Regionally, EMEA pricing accelerated to +2.4% on laundry pods, capturing 60% pass-through of soda ash costs while preserving 85% household retention rates. North America was more measured at +1.4%, focusing on everyday low pricing to defend against Amazon Basics encroachment. Our pricing engine, powered by real-time consumer scanner data from NielsenIQ and proprietary elasticity models, ensured we avoided the volume erosion seen in P&G's fabric care reset last year. Net-net, pricing funded 40% of our input cost inflation absorption, keeping gross margins stable at 48.2%.

Favorable mix of +1.3% was our secret sauce, driven by premiumization—a CPG megatrend we're leaning into hard. This was worth nearly 25% of total organic growth and improved from +0.9% in Q1. Premium products, now 42% of sales up from 38% YoY, grew 9% versus flat mass tiers. In Snacks, trading consumers up to IndulgePro gourmet clusters +18% growth from standard chips offset a -2% dip in value bags. Personal Care mix shifted +1.8% via EcoGlow sustainable skincare, which commands 20% price premiums and aligns with Nielsen's 2024 sustainability report showing 65% of millennials prioritizing green claims.

Asia-Pacific mix popped +2.1% on jumbo-pack multipacks in Indonesia, while Latin America's +0.8% reflected strong hygiene product uptake post-dengue outbreaks. Strategic enablers include our Portfolio Powerhouse initiative: pruning 12% of low-velocity SKUs echoing Colgate's playbook, reallocating to high-growth adjacencies like plant-based beverages, which now contribute +0.6 points to mix. This not only boosts revenue per case but lifts segment margins by 120 basis points through better fixed cost leverage.

This decomposition validates our Growth Through Precision strategy: volume from executional excellence, pricing from data-led discipline, and mix from relentless innovation. We're not chasing short-term wins like some peers' aggressive hikes that risk share loss; instead, we're building moats via 25+ new product launches this year, including RTD coffees targeting Starbucks' at-home shift. Regionally, we see North America sustaining +4-6% organic, EMEA +3-5% amid stabilizing inflation, and high-teens upside in Asia/LATAM from urbanization tails.

Now, turning to geographic performance, which highlights the divergent dynamics shaping our strategy across developed and emerging markets. Total net sales grew 5.2% on a reported basis to $12.8 billion, with organic growth of 4.1% at constant currency—though our overall organic was stronger at 5.2% factoring in all elements.

Developed markets, accounting for 58% of total sales or $7.4 billion, grew 2.8% organically, slightly ahead of our guidance midpoint. North America, 32% of group sales, was the standout at 4.2% organic growth driven by premiumization in Home Care and Beauty. Our Tide Pods and Ariel 3-in-1 laundry capsules saw 7% volume uplift from innovation in concentrated formats and eco-friendly variants, capturing share per IRI data. Pricing contributed 3.5 points to offset 4-6% input cost inflation on surfactants and packaging resins.

Europe, at 18% of sales, grew a modest 1.9% organically amid softer consumer sentiment and regulatory headwinds. Fabric Care volumes dipped 1% due to downtrading in laundry detergents, but Beauty held firm with 3% growth, led by Pantene Pro-V repair lines and Olay Regenerist skincare, gaining 1.2 points of market share per Kantar Worldpanel. Japan and Australia were flat, countered by SKU rationalization—we've pruned 15% of low-velocity SKUs in Fabric & Home Care to focus on high-margin heroes.

Emerging markets, 42% of sales or $5.4 billion, roared ahead with 6.7% organic growth—more than double developed markets and aligning with our mid-single-digit CAGR target through 2027. Asia-Pacific, 22% of group sales, surged 9.1%, propelled by volume expansion in Snacks and Personal Care. In China, despite macro challenges like 15% youth unemployment, our Lay's premium baked variants and Head & Shoulders anti-dandruff shampoos posted 12% growth, gaining distribution in 5,000 additional hypermarkets via Alibaba's Freshippo and JD.com. India delivered 11% growth with Dove body washes and Lux soaps expanding into Tier-2/3 cities through Project Shakti—our micro-entrepreneur model now reaching 1.2 million rural outlets, boosting rural penetration by 8 points per Nielsen.

Latin America grew 5.2%, resilient against currency volatility; Brazil's Magnum ice cream impulse line and Downy fabric enhancers offset a 2% volume dip in Beverages from unseasonal weather. Africa/Middle East was at 4.8% growth, where Royco soups and Omo laundry bars gained traction in urbanizing markets like Nigeria, with e-commerce up 25% YoY via Jumia integrations.

Key trends: Developed markets faced U.S. CPI at 3.2% pressuring value-seekers, leading to a 2-point mix shift toward mid-tier—but premium shelf-space investments yielded 1.5 points of market share gain. Emerging markets benefited from 1.5% real GDP growth outpacing developed peers, though forex shaved 150 basis points off reported; at constant currency, EM organic was 8.2%. Supply chain localization pays off: In India and Indonesia, we've localized 70% of PET resin production, cutting logistics by 12% and insulating against Red Sea issues.

Strategically, our Emerging First playbook allocates 65% of $2.1 billion FY capex to EM infrastructure—like new blending plants in Vietnam for beverages and R&D hubs in São Paulo for tropical skincare. Digitally, Always On e-commerce drives 18% of EM sales, up from 12%, mirroring P&G's China approach. Sustainability: 50% recycled plastic in EM packaging boosted brand love scores by 10 points in Nielsen surveys.

Looking forward, developed markets at 2-4% organic in FY24 with pricing moderating to 2 points; emerging at 7-9%, vigilant on China stimulus and LatAm elections. This balance positions us to outperform Unilever and Colgate at 5%+ group organic.

As we turn to outlook, I'm pleased to share our organic sales growth guidance for the remainder of fiscal 2024 and into Q1 of 2025, against a CPG landscape navigating sticky inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and competition from national brands and private labels.

For full FY2024, we're raising guidance to 4% to 6%, up from 3% to 5%. This reflects stronger-than-expected pricing in the first half, capturing +520 basis points net pricing YoY, offsetting raw material headwinds in edible oils and PET resin. Volume/mix now flat to +1%, improved from prior, driven by distribution and innovation.

By driver: Pricing targets +300 to 400 bps, elasticity -2.5 to -3.0—better than -3.5 in 2022 peak, mirroring P&G and Colgate-Palmolive EDLP stabilizing penetration. Volume/Mix: Premiumization accelerating, high-margin Vitality portfolio—including plant-based QuickBite snacks and clean beauty FreshGlow—delivering +8% mix uplift. Value segments pressured by Aldi/Lidl, countered by loyalty and shopper marketing.

Regionally: North America (55% sales) 5% to 7%, fueled by e-commerce—DTC up 25% Q2—and health & wellness velocity. IRI shows 50 bps gain in household care vs. Kimberly-Clark via PureHome eco-refills tapping 15% CAGR sustainable packaging. Europe (25%) 2% to 4%, muted by energy costs; countering UK/Germany promotions where Nielsen indicates flat fabric care volume amid Unilever pushback. Emerging (15%) 6% to 8%, led by India/Brazil. India QuickBite savory snacks outpace Nestlé Maggi +12% volume from rural Project Shakti to 1.2 million outlets. LatAm currency-neutral beverage pricing despite FX.

For Q3—seasonally soft—3% to 5% organic, embedding +250 bps pricing and flat volumes, tougher comps from last year's launches. Q1 FY25 early at 4% to 6%, assuming no cocoa/palm oil escalation post-40% spikes lapped.

Pillars: 1. Innovation: 20+ launches, AI-optimized FreshGlow microbiome skincare targeting $50B beauty actives at 7% CAGR per Euromonitor. 2. Supply chain: SAP S/4HANA NA go-live cut inventory days 15%, better service amid ports; precision ag hedges 30% ag inputs. 3. Agility: Digital shelf analytics, zero-based media for ROIC >15% core SKUs; divesting low-single-digit brands for functional nutrition M&A like Mondelez.

Confident in through-P&L leverage, adjusted EPS growth 6% to 8% FY24 midpoint.

That wraps up the financial details. Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then 1. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your consumer spending habits?

Mike Reynolds:
Good morning, John. Inflation continues to pressure value-conscious consumers, leading to some downtrading in developed markets like Europe where we've seen softer volumes in fabric care. However, our balanced approach—affordable premium tiers like $4.99 VivaSnax multipacks growing 25%, disciplined EDLP, and premiumization in health & wellness—has driven volume up 2.1% overall. In emerging markets, real GDP growth and urbanization tails provide tailwinds, with strong execution in India via Project Shakti offsetting any macro softness. We're gaining share per Nielsen and IRI, positioning us well as inflation moderates.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.

Emily Chen:
Regarding your new product HydraSpark, what are the projections for its market impact?

Tom Vargas:
Thanks, Emily. HydraSpark has been a breakout, with Q2 velocity up 12% in North America, capturing share from flat soda volumes at PepsiCo peers. Projections: we'll scale to +3.5% NARTD volume contribution in H2, targeting 5% market share in sparkling water by year-end via e-commerce and convenience channel gains. Globally, expect mid-teens growth into FY25, funding marketing with modest pricing while aligning with zero-sugar trends—early signs show 2x ROI on influencer campaigns.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Lisa Chen:
Hi David. Promotional spending was managed tightly at 18% of sales, flat YoY, with 2.5x ROI via our Velocity Accelerator—AI planogramming boosted facings 8%, driving 2.1% volume. We focused on high-ROI tactics like in-store demos for NutriCrunch (15% penetration gain) and targeted UK/Germany promos countering private labels. This funded 40% of cost inflation absorption, stable margins at 48.2%, and mix uplift—pruning 12-15% low-velocity SKUs per Portfolio Powerhouse. Efficiency gains from SAP and demand sensing keep us agile without excess spend.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Mike Reynolds for closing remarks.

Mike Reynolds:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders, backed by accelerating organic growth, geographic balance, and precision execution. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Decomposition of organic sales growth: volume, price, mix
Organic sales growth guidance for next quarter/year
Geographic performance: developed vs. emerging markets

aspect_summary.Decomposition of organic sales growth: v: Q2 organic sales growth of 5.2% decomposed into +2.1% volume (strongest in two years, broad-based across categories/regions), +1.8% net pricing (disciplined, below category average), and +1.3% favorable mix shift (driven by premiumization, premium products now 42% of sales).
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth guidance for next q: FY2024 raised to 4-6% (from 3-5%), with pricing +3-4%, volume/mix flat to +1%; Q3 3-5% (soft seasonality, +2.5% pricing, flat volumes); Q1 FY2025 4-6%; second half and FY2025 sustaining 4-6%, volume to 2.5%+.
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth rate: Q2 5.2% (ahead of 3-5% guidance, third consecutive quarter of acceleration); H1 YTD 4.8%; on track for FY2024 4-6%.
aspect_summary.Geographic performance: developed vs. em: Developed markets (58% sales, $7.4B): +2.8% organic (North America 5.1%, Europe/EMEA 3.7%/1.9%); Emerging markets (42% sales, $5.4B): +6.7% organic (Latin America 7.4%/5.2%, Asia-Pacific 2.9%/9.1%).
